title: Outlook: Copilot summaries at the top of search results, with a link into Copilot chat
summary: Pass. The roadmap facts and both admin paths are supported, while the card's default, licence tier and dedicated controls remain explicitly uncertain. A minor clarification should acknowledge Microsoft's conflicting descriptions of whether Integrated Apps blocking affects Teams.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No dedicated UI setting or API for showing or hiding just the Outlook search-summary card is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook search summary card Copilot disable admin setting Exchange PowerShell; "Outlook" "search" "summary card". Read Manage Copilot Chat, cross-application app controls and package block/update references; none documents a switch or call for this card alone.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[2].governs; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Copilot integrated app provides Copilot Chat in Outlook across web, desktop and mobile, and administrators can manage its availability.
claims.quote: The Copilot app is an integrated app that provides Copilot Chat via web, in the Microsoft Copilot app (web, desktop, mobile) and in Outlook (web, desktop, mobile). Admins can deploy the Copilot app or manage its availability.

claims.claim: The block control is in Microsoft 365 admin center at Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps. Select the Available Apps list. Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane. Select Block app.

claims.claim: An API equivalent explicitly documented to block the Copilot app itself through Integrated Apps has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Integrated Apps Copilot block app user availability Microsoft Graph API PowerShell Exchange; "Integrated apps" "Copilot" "Graph" "block". Read package block, resource and list references: agent/tool packages are covered, but the Copilot app itself is not identified.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Group availability is set in Microsoft 365 admin center at Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Users > Specific users/group in the organization can install.
claims.quote: Select Settings, then select Integrated Apps. Select the Available Apps list. Next, select the app you want to edit. ... select the Users tab in the overview pane. ... Specific users/group in the organization can install

claims.claim: An API explicitly documented to set Integrated Apps user/group availability for the Copilot app itself is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Integrated apps" "availability" "API" "users"; "Copilot" "Integrated Apps" "PowerShell" "availability"; "copilotPackage" "update" "availability". Read package update/resource/list references; they don't establish that the Copilot app itself is a managed package.

claims.where: controls[1].note; controls[2].note; Scope: Roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented Integrated Apps controls are only available to Global Administrators.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins. Check your credentials before you proceed.

claims.claim: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps blocks it in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook and Copilot Chat on the web.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.
claims.fix: After the cross-client blocking statement, add: "Microsoft's general cross-application apps guidance says blocking affects only Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application, with Teams continuing to honour Teams admin center settings; this differs from the Copilot-specific guidance above." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365#how-to-block-an-app. Retain the supported Copilot-specific statement.

claims.claim: Blocking the Copilot app also blocks users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: If you block the Copilot app using the Integrated app control, you block the Copilot app tenant-wide across the Microsoft Copilot app, Outlook, and the web, including for users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: Blocking an app overrides previous administrator deployments and user installations.
claims.quote: Blocking an app overrides any previous admin deployment or user installation in Microsoft 365 and Outlook so that no one in your organization can use the app.

claims.claim: Block app is an organisation-wide control affecting all users.
claims.quote: When you choose to block an app, it is blocked for all users in your organization.

claims.claim: Specific users/group availability permits only the selected users to self-install the app from the store and use it.
claims.quote: Specific users/group in the organization can install means that only the users selected by you are able to install the app on their own from the store and use it in the client. Unselected users are not able to do so.

claims.claim: App availability settings do not affect administrator-deployed apps.
claims.quote: The availability setting of an app doesn't impact any admin deployed apps. The availability setting only allows you to control which end users can install and use these apps on their own. Any previous admin deployments made are still be honored.

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests assigning a group containing only licensed users to keep the Copilot app out of the store for unlicensed users.
claims.quote: To prevent the Copilot app from being available in the App store for unlicensed users, select Specific users/group in the organization can install and assign a group that includes only licensed users.

claims.claim: The Integrated Apps Copilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and the Copilot Chat apps.
claims.quote: On the Integrated Apps page, the CoPilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and the Copilot Chat apps. Any changes made to this app from the integrated apps portal apply to both.
